headline: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO with Colette Kress as interim, and the market absorbed it (S&P -0.4%) while 10-year yields posted their biggest surge since 2022.
regime: The key-person shock landed and did not break the tape: S&P -0.4%, Semis ETF -1.0% on the day but +12.1% on five days, VIX 18.4 (-28% on five days). Rates are the real headwind: the 10-year is at 5.1% with Fed hikes being priced and BofA's Hartnett says stay risk-off until yields fall below 4.5%. Within AI the money keeps rotating away from Nvidia toward AMD/Broadcom and toward equipment and cooling, while leveraged neoclouds (Nebius -20%, CoreWeave -7%) take the punishment.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Samsung is reportedly in talks to buy Modine for AI cooling; MOD +28% (b82cf021486d, ca310f9d0c49)
Constellation +13% in a week on its second guidance raise this year (b962a2ecb79e); Oracle now books $16bn a year per gigawatt (a86f331cceb6)
Cooling +21.9% and power +16.5% on five days (digest segments)
Against: GE Vernova and Vertiv fell 12% in the week to Nov 10 on data-centre backlash (ab88af424ac8); power -2.1% on the day
theses.change_note: A strategic bid for Modine and Constellation's raise support it, but power/grid lagged compute and equipment on five days and the backlash selloff is real; net flat.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Applied Materials beat Q4 estimates and rose as CoreWeave's results eased hardware-demand fears (ecf89f0d6add, cba5b7fa705e)
Oracle's revenue per gigawatt rose 60% to $16bn on new AI contracts (a86f331cceb6); Coherent signed a $20bn AI customer deal (514334f7652b)
CoreWeave and Cisco results boosted AI sentiment (61fc602352ce)
Against: Burry warns of a coming chip glut (41d14b55338c); Oracle's backlog is about half OpenAI, which lost ~$13.5bn in Q3 (e34c4cd3f36f)
theses.change_note: +2: AMAT's beat, Oracle's pricing and Coherent's deal are hard demand data; the OpenAI concentration risk caps it.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: Nebius fell ~20% after raising capex plans to $45bn and pushing revenue into 2027 (7fb5bb45d9c3, 194b5a850cb2)
CoreWeave sank ~7% after Huang's exit raised doubts about its biggest supplier and ally (752c03210070, 5d2698e583be)
Segment -4.1% on the day, the worst; all five neoclouds fail the quality gate (shortlist)
Against: Oppenheimer keeps a $150 target on CoreWeave (cd0d5087c368)
theses.change_note: +2: Nebius's capex jump is exactly the debt-funded overreach the thesis describes, and the Nvidia shock hit this segment hardest.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Sandisk trades at 3.2x forward earnings with an 8% FCF yield and 73% operating margin; WDC at 7.7x (shortlist)
Memory +17.8% on five days; Micron is committing ~$1bn to Anthropic's placement as a key HBM supplier (digest segments, 91a51fa603be)
Against: -24.6% on the month and Micron moves 5%+ on a third of days (724128a09b2b); one buyer holds off on Sandisk above $900 (928b5b9fc2ad)
theses.change_note: +4: the bounce held for a full week (+17.8%) rather than one day, which was yesterday's test; volatility keeps confidence below 50.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Oracle's backlog is about half OpenAI, which could only 'scrape together $11bn' (e34c4cd3f36f); Oracle fails the cash-flow quality gate (shortlist)
Alphabet is borrowing to fund AI (prior worldview)
Against: hyperscalers are the steadiest AI segment, +3.9% on five days (digest segments)
theses.change_note: +1: Oracle's dependence on a loss-making customer shows how capex is being financed on promises, not cash.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: Bond yields saw their biggest surge since 2022 on Fed-hike expectations; 10-year 5.1% (30f9a5f61b8d, digest tape)
Hartnett: stay risk-off until yields fall below 4.5% (17e7048a2862); Bitcoin broke $70k on $1bn of liquidations (a925682c06d7)
Against: VIX -28% on five days and Wells Fargo dropped its call to avoid AI infrastructure (681d832f7613)
theses.change_note: +1: rates keep rising and leveraged speculation (crypto) is unwinding; the AI tape's resilience is the only counterpoint.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress raises policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: GE Vernova and Vertiv fell 12% in a week as data-centre backlash hit AI power after the midterms (ab88af424ac8)
Texas data-centre regulations are weighing on Nebius (8202d87e0c06); Washington may tighten chip export controls (6be2e16a8c7c)
Against: no moratorium has passed; grid +13.4% on five days (digest segments)
theses.change_note: +2: the backlash now shows in prices of the power suppliers and Texas rules are cited as a live drag.

theses.title: The Huang probe puts Nvidia, and China export rules, at risk
evidence: Huang resigned; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO (61fc602352ce, ff5f3a08ae53)
Banned Nvidia chips traced to a China data centre linked to Alice Huang; DOJ probing Super Micro smuggling (8fb9d2f57faf, 72f4186e8de3, d9897c8e452b)
AMD +44.7% vs NVDA -8.5% on five days (digest segments, 376969b970a5)
Against: the market weathered the exit and NVDA rose 2.3% premarket; Yardeni calls it a buying opportunity (964388513fa8, ca87f4eccd47, 6be2e16a8c7c)
theses.change_note: +5: the ouster happened and the scandal widened to export violations, which invites tighter controls; the key-person part is now realised, the export part is growing.

compute.note: AMD +44.7% and NVDA -8.5% on five days; rivals gain what Nvidia loses, but export risk hangs over all.

foundry_equipment.note: +20.6% on five days; AMAT beat Q4. Still -19.2% on the month.

memory_storage.note: Upgraded from underweight: +17.8% on five days held the bounce; Sandisk at 3.2x forward earnings.

networking_optical.note: +25.2% on five days, COHR's $20bn deal; -25.6% on the month.

servers.note: -28.0% on the month; Super Micro DOJ smuggling probe adds to Nvidia-tie risk.

power_nuclear.note: Constellation's guidance raise; -2.1% on the day and backlash risk.

grid_electrical.note: +13.4% on five days; GE Vernova's backlash drop is the warning.

cooling_thermal.note: +21.9% on five days, AAON +44.8%; Samsung eyeing Modine shows strategic value.

datacenter_neocloud.note: -4.1% on the day; Nebius -20% on a $45bn capex plan, CoreWeave hit by Huang's exit.

hyperscalers.note: +3.9% on five days; Oracle's OpenAI-heavy backlog and Microsoft's outage.

ai_software.note: -21.7% on the month; nothing in the news to change it.

risks: Tighter chip export controls after the China smuggling revelations would hit Nvidia, equipment and servers together.
The 10-year above 5% with Fed hikes priced could drag every long-duration AI name.
OpenAI's losses threaten Oracle's backlog and, through it, data-centre and power orders.
A Texas or federal data-centre moratorium would hit power, grid, cooling and servers at once.
Neocloud financing stress (Nebius, CoreWeave) could spread to their suppliers' order books.
watch: Nvidia's first full session under interim CEO Kress and any news on a permanent CEO.
Any Commerce Department move on export controls after the smuggling reports.
10-year yield vs 5.1% and Fed speakers on December hikes.
Whether Samsung confirms a Modine bid and how cooling peers reprice.
Whether memory holds its five-day gain after Friday's -1.9%.
